title: FIFO versus LRU
description: The same five loads under *FIFO* and under *LRU*, and where they differ.

steps.text: This cache replaces with *FIFO*: first in, first out. It evicts the line that arrived earliest, and a hit does not change that order. The trace loads `0x000`, `0x040`, `0x000`, `0x080` and `0x000`; all five map to set 0, which has two ways. Under FIFO, how many of the five loads will hit?
steps.explain: One. The third load hits, but it does not make `0x000` any newer. When `0x080` arrives, `0x000` is still the first in, so it is evicted, and the last load misses.
steps.hint: A hit does not change the order of arrival. Which line arrived first?
Press Run in the transport bar. If the trace has already run, press Reset, then Run.

steps.text: One hit, four misses. Loading `0x080` evicted `0x000`, the line the program had just used, and the last load had to bring it back in.
Set Replacement to LRU. The cache will ask to reset; choose Reset and apply.
steps.hint: Replacement is in the bar above the cache. Pick LRU.
Press Run in the transport bar.

steps.text: Two hits. Under LRU the third load made `0x000` the most recent, so `0x080` evicted `0x040` instead and the last load hit. Replacement should follow how a line is used, not when it arrived.
